title: Level Order Values
statement:
List a binary tree's values one depth level at a time.

Contract
- `root` may be null. Nodes have an integer `value` and nullable `left` and `right` children.
- Return a list with one inner list per level, starting with the root's level. Within a level, list values from left to right.
- A null tree returns an empty outer list. Levels never appear empty. Do not modify the tree.
- Trees may be lopsided, with a height of up to 1000 nodes.

Examples
- `[1, 2, 3, 4, null, null, 5]` returns `[[1], [2, 3], [4, 5]]`.
- A null tree returns `[]`.
- `[7]` returns `[[7]]`.
hints: Nodes at the same depth must be reported together, so a plain depth-first walk in the usual order is not enough by itself.
Keep a queue of the nodes on the current level. Before expanding it, note how many nodes it holds, then take exactly that many, record their values, and enqueue their children.
Each node is enqueued and dequeued once. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for n nodes, since the output and queue together hold every node.
inputSyntax: Input: the tree in level order with null for missing children, for example: [1, 2, 3, 4, null, null, 5]
